```{r setup, message=F, warning=F}
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(svglite)
library(htmltools)
source("../../../prep (May 2025).r")
theme_set(base_quarto)

no_lead <- function(x, digits = 2) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", as.character(round(x, digits)))

fmt_feats <- function(x, col_widths = list(description = 2.5, 
                                           feature = .6, 
                                           scoring = 1, 
                                           range = 0.8)) {
  if (!inherits(x, "flextable")) x <- flextable(x)
  present <- names(x$body$dataset)
  for (col in intersect(names(col_widths), present)) {
    x <- flextable::width(x, j = col, width = col_widths[[col]])
  }
  x |>
    height_all(height = 0.5, part = "body") |>
    hrule(rule = "exact", part = "body") |>
    set_table_properties(layout = "fixed") |>
    add_footer_lines("Ranges are per-game averages from training runs; per-position values can be wider.")
}
```

```{r engine-setup, include=FALSE}
engine    <- reticulate::import_from_path("engine", path = "../python/Temporal Difference")
chess_m   <- reticulate::import("chess")
chess_svg <- reticulate::import("chess.svg")
```

```{r render-ply-fn, include=FALSE}
# render_ply: produces a side-by-side board SVG + diverging bar chart
# showing feature values, weights, and contributions at a given ply.
render_ply <- function(board, feat_col, wt_col, feats_df = feats, wts_df = wts) {
  vals    <- as.numeric(feats_df[[feat_col]])
  wts_vec <- as.numeric(wts_df[[wt_col]])

  chart_data <- tibble(
    feature      = feats_df$feature,
    value        = vals,
    weight       = wts_vec,
    contribution = vals * wts_vec
  ) |>
    pivot_longer(c(value, weight, contribution),
                 names_to  = "metric",
                 values_to = "val") |>
    mutate(
      metric  = factor(metric,
                       levels = c("value", "weight", "contribution"),
                       labels = c("Feature value", "Weight", "Contribution")),
      feature = factor(feature, levels = rev(feats_df$feature))
    )

  p <- ggplot(chart_data, aes(x = val, y = feature, fill = val > 0)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.55) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.35, color = "grey40") +
    facet_wrap(~metric, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("TRUE" = "#2166ac", "FALSE" = "#d6604d"),
      guide  = "none"
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8)
    )

  board_svg   <- chess_svg$board(board, size = 220L)
  chart_svg_s <- svglite::stringSVG({ print(p) }, width = 5.5, height = 1.8)

  htmltools::div(
    style = "display:flex; gap:20px; align-items:center; margin:16px 0 28px;",
    htmltools::div(
      style = "flex: 0 0 220px;",
      htmltools::HTML(board_svg)
    ),
    htmltools::div(
      style = "flex: 1; min-width: 0;",
      htmltools::HTML(chart_svg_s)
    )
  )
}
```

## Overview

This document walks through the engine's learning process in detail,
using a single short chess game as a concrete example. By the end you
should understand:

- What a **weight** is and what it represents
- How the engine **evaluates** a board position using those weights
- How a game's result is used to **update** the weights via temporal
  difference learning
- Why some concepts (like queen value) are learned faster than others

## Game

We'll use Scholar's Mate — a four-move checkmate — as our example. It's
short enough to trace every step, and it has a decisive result (white
wins), which produces a clear learning signal.

The moves are: **1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nc6 3. Qh5 Nf6?? 4. Qxf7#**

White wins by exploiting the weakness of black's f7 square. King safety
is the critical factor in this game — the engine should learn that from
these four positions.

```{r import-game, include=FALSE}
embed_url <- "https://lichess.org/embed/game/9VP5REFK?theme=auto&bg=auto"
```

```{r show-game, include=TRUE}
htmltools::tags$iframe(
  src    = embed_url,
  width  = "100%",
  height = "450px",
  style  = "border: none;"
)
```

## Evaluation

The engine knows nothing about chess strategy on its own. It knows the
rules of the game and a handful of features of any board position. The
engine then combines the board features into a single score using a
weighted sum:

$$\text{score} = w_1 \times feature_1 + w_2 \times feature_2 + \cdots + w_n \times feature_n$$

The board features and how they are scored are fixed. What changes are
the weights, which update after each move and in response to the game
outcome. After lots of games, the weights should come to reflect the
true value of each board feature in the game of chess. As the engine's
weights get closer to each feature's true value in the game of chess,
its ability to play the game of chess improves.

A positive score means the position looks good for the side to move;
negative means it looks bad. After white moves, the evaluation score is
from black's perspective.

Let's learn from this game. First, we set the engine.

Let's start an object to collect the feature values at each half-move
('ply')

```{r}
set.seed(3453)
feats <- tibble(feature_name=names(engine$default_weights("zero")),
                feature=c("Passed pawn",
                          "Doubled pawn",
                          "Isolated pawn",
                          "Backward pawn",
                          "King safety",
                          "Center control",
                          "Rook open file",
                          "Connected rooks",
                          "Knight outpost",
                          "Bishop pair",
                          "Rook seventh rank",
                          "Piece development",
                          "Mobility",
                          "Pawn advancement"),
                description = c(
                    "Pawns with no opposing pawns ahead on same/adjacent file",
                    "Extra pawns beyond one on any file (penalty)",
                    "Pawns with no friendly pawns on adjacent files (penalty)",
                    "Pawns that cannot advance safely — sentry pawn ahead (penalty)",
                    "Friendly pawns 1-2 ranks ahead of king, minus pieces attacking king zone",
                    "Central squares (d4, d5, e4, e5) attacked or occupied",
                    "Rooks on files with no pawns of either color",
                    "Both rooks share a rank/file with no pieces between",
                    "Knights on strong central squares (piece-square table)",
                    "Having both bishops vs. opponent",
                    "Rooks on the 7th rank (2nd rank for black)",
                    "Minor pieces off their starting squares",
                    "Squares attacked by all non-king pieces (normalized)",
                    "Total rank advancement of all pawns from starting rank (normalized)"),
                divisor = c(
                    "none",
                    "none",
                    "none",
                    "none",
                    "/3",
                    "/4",
                    "none",
                    "none",
                    "/2",
                    "none",
                    "none",
                    "none",
                    "/30",
                    "/20"
                ),
                scoring = c(
                    rep("Our count minus theirs", 4),
                    rep("Our count minus theirs", 4),
                    "Our score minus theirs",
                    "1/0 -- our minus theirs",
                    rep("Our count minus theirs", 2),
                    rep("Our count minus theirs (normalized)", 2)),
                range = c(
                    "[-5, +5]",     # passed_pawn
                    "[-2, +2]",     # doubled_pawn
                    "[-4, +5]",     # isolated_pawn
                    "[-2, +2]",     # backward_pawn
                    "[-5, +5]",     # king_safety
                    "[-3, +3]",     # center_control
                    "[-2, +2]",     # rook_open_file
                    "[-1, +1]",     # connected_rooks
                    "[-0.4, +0.4]", # knight_pst
                    "[-1, +1]",     # bishop_pair
                    "[-1, +1]",     # rook_seventh
                    "[-3, +3]",     # piece_development
                    "[-19, +20]",   # mobility
                    "[-9, +15]"     # pawn_advancement
                ))


feats %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

The starting weight values are just randomly seeded to jumpstart the learning process. 

For Scholar's Mate, the most meaningful features the engine can learn from are center control, king safety, and piece development. Our features table will be trimmed to just these three.

```{r}
set.seed(432)
featsSch <- feats %>%
    .[c(6,5,12),] 

featsSch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

We'll start by creating an object to store the feature values and weights for each half-move (ply). 

```{r}
set.seed(32)
sch <- featsSch %>%
    mutate(f0=0,
           w0 = abs(round(rnorm(3, 0, .01), 4))) %>%
# random starting weight to jumpstart learning
# constrained to be positive, because we know that all features are constructed to be positive)
select(feature_name, feature, f0, w0)

sch %>%
    flextable()
```

The overall evaluation score is the sum of all scores for each feature evalation

```{r}
# State before ply 1 (starting position)
score_t <- sum(sch$f0 * sch$w0)
score_t
```

We've set the initial feature values, the initial weights, and the initial score. Note that all feature values, weights, and scores are from the point of view of the player to move. So time zero is the start of the game before any moves. All values, weights, and scores at an even numbered ply are from the point of view of white. All values, weights, and scores at odd-numbered plys are from the point of view of black. 

We will now set up a board, make a move, and do the following: 

- Update the feature values
- Calculate evaluation score


(1) update the feature
values, 
(2) calculate the evaluation score based on the updated feature
values and the weights from the previous move, and 
(3) update the
weights using the evaluation score, the error, the learning rate, and
the weights from the previous move.

Each move section ends with a panel showing the board alongside a
diverging bar chart of **feature values**, **weights**, and
**contributions** (value × weight) at that moment. Blue bars are
positive; red bars are negative.

### 1. e4

Play first ply and update the feature values

```{r}
# Fresh board
b   <- chess_m$Board()
b
# Push 1.e4 and evaluate next state
b$push(chess_m$Move$from_uci("e2e4"))
b

sch <- sch %>%
    mutate(f1 = as.numeric(
        reticulate::py_to_r(
            engine$extract_features(b))[sch$feature_name]))

sch %>%
    fmt_feats
```

White both attacks and occupies the center! This is negative 1 for black on center control, which with the scaling comes to -.5. A pawn was removed from the King's shield, so white gets dinged on king safety. There is no change to piece development. 

We score the position by summing the products of feature values and the previous move's weights

```{r}
score_t1 <- sum(sch$f1 * sch$w0)
score_t1
```

The score `r score_t1` is from black's point of view. So after white
plays e4, black has a slightly better position due to white's weaker King. But really this is just
noise after a single move with randomly seeded weights.

Let's update the weights based on the new score and the new feature
values.

```{r}
lr    <- 0.1
error <- score_t1 - score_t

sch <- sch %>%
    mutate(w1 = round(sch$w0 + lr * error * sch$f1,4))

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

After e4, the weights on central control and piece development slightly increased.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(render_ply(b, "f1", "w1", feats_df = sch, wts_df = sch))
```

### 1. ... e5

```{r}
b$push(chess_m$Move$from_uci("e7e5"))

sch$f2 <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(engine$extract_features(b))[sch$feature_name])

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

Now black is attacking a central square! This brings the feature value
back to zero.

```{r}
score_t2 <- sum(sch$w1 * sch$f2)
score_t2
```

Which brings the evaluation score back to zero. It's white's move, so
the score reflects white's point of view.

```{r}
error  <- score_t2 - score_t1

sch <- sch %>%
    mutate(w2 = w1 + lr * error * f2)

sch %>% 
    fmt_feats()
```

The feature values were all zero, so the weights do not change for this
update.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(render_ply(b, "f2", "w2", feats_df = sch, wts_df = sch))
```

### 2. Bc4

```{r}
b$push(chess_m$Move$from_uci("f1c4"))

sch$f3 <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(engine$extract_features(b))[sch$feature_name])

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

f7 is attacked! Black's feature evaluations of king safety and piece development take damage! 

```{r}
score_t3 <- sum(sch$w2 * sch$f3)
score_t3
```

After Bc4, the engine thinks black is a little worse than it had been.

```{r}
error  <- score_t3 - score_t2

sch <- sch %>%
    mutate(w3 = round(w2 + lr * error * f3, 4))

sch %>% 
    fmt_feats()
```

The weight on king safety slightly increased.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(render_ply(b, "f3", "w3", feats_df = sch, wts_df = sch))
```

### 2. ... Nc6

```{r}
b$push(chess_m$Move$from_uci("b8c6"))

sch$f4 <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(engine$extract_features(b))[sch$feature_name])

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

Black's knight move added another attack on the center. From white's
point of view, she is winning on king safety and losing on central
control.

```{r}
score_t4 <- sum(sch$w3 * sch$f4)
score_t4
```

The engine thinks white is slightly better.

```{r}
error  <- score_t4 - score_t3

sch <- sch %>%
    mutate(w4 = round(w3 + lr * error * f4, 4))

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

The weight for king safety got stronger, while the weight on center
control actually turned negative — clearly wrong, but it makes sense
from the engine's point of view. Black is winning on center control but
the overall score favors white. Therefore, center control is correlated
with losing. The engine needs lots of games to learn that center control
is correlated with winning.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(render_ply(b, "f4", "w4", feats_df = sch, wts_df = sch))
```

### 3. Qh5

```{r}
b$push(chess_m$Move$from_uci("d1h5"))

sch$f5 <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(engine$extract_features(b))[sch$feature_name])

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

```{r}
score_t5 <- sum(sch$w4 * sch$f5)
score_t5
```

Black's position continues to worsen.

```{r}
error  <- score_t5 - score_t4

sch <- sch %>%
    mutate(w5 = round(w4 + lr * error * f5, 4))

sch %>% 
    fmt_feats()
```

The weight for king safety increases.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(render_ply(b, "f5", "w5", feats_df = sch, wts_df = sch))
```

### 3. ... Nf6

```{r}
b$push(chess_m$Move$from_uci("g8f6"))

sch$f6 <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(engine$extract_features(b))[sch$feature_name])

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

The knight move attacks two more center squares.

```{r}
score_t6 <- sum(sch$w5 * sch$f6)
score_t6
```

White's position continues to improve.

```{r}
error  <- score_t6 - score_t5

sch <- sch %>%
    mutate(w6 = round(w5 + lr * error * f6, 4))

sch %>% 
    fmt_feats()
```

Same trend — stronger negative weight for center control and stronger
positive weight for king safety.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(render_ply(b, "f6", "w6", feats_df = sch, wts_df = sch))
```

### 4. Qxf7# 

```{r}
b$push(chess_m$Move$from_uci("h5f7"))

sch$f7 <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(engine$extract_features(b))[sch$feature_name])

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

From black's point of view, he's winning the center but did not see to
his king safety.

```{r}
score_t7 <- sum(sch$w6 * sch$f7)
score_t7
```

Black's position worsens.

When we did not have the outcome of the game as our target, we used the
previous move's score as the benchmark to measure error against. Now
that we have an outcome of black losing, we assign a -1 and generate
our errors from that benchmark.

```{r}
target <- -1                          # black is to move and has lost
error  <- target - score_t7

sch <- sch %>% 
    mutate(w7 = round(w6 + lr * error * f7, 4))

sch %>%
    fmt_feats()
```

Note what learning has taken place after this game. Black was winning
the center but lost. Therefore, the engine thinks control of the center
is correlated with losing in general. Black lost the game on king
safety, so that gets a correct and relatively high weight.

It's unclear whether a run of Scholar's Mate games would correct the
engine's mistaken impression that center control is bad.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(render_ply(b, "f7", "w7", feats_df = sch, wts_df = sch))
```

## Review 

Let's plot the trajectory of feature values, scores, and weights across
the full game.

### Score trajectory

The engine score at each ply, converted to a consistent white-advantage
scale (positive = white winning). Points are colored by whose turn it
is at that moment.

```{r}
traj <- tibble(
  ply       = 0:7,
  label     = c("Start", "1.e4", "1...e5", "2.Bc4", "2...Nc6",
                "3.Qh5", "3...Nf6", "4.Qxf7#"),
  raw_score = c(score_t, score_t1, score_t2, score_t3,
                score_t4, score_t5, score_t6, score_t7),
  to_move   = rep(c("White", "Black"), 4)
) |>
  # Convert to white's perspective: negate when it's black to move
  mutate(
    white_adv = if_else(to_move == "White", raw_score, -raw_score),
    label     = factor(label, levels = label)
  )
traj %>%
    flextable()
```

```{r}
ggplot(traj, aes(x = label, y = white_adv, group = 1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60",
             linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(color = to_move), size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("White" = "#8B4513", "Black" = "#D2B48C")) +
  annotate("text", x = 8.3, y = 0.05, label = "+1 (white wins)",
           hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey40") +
  labs(
    title  = "Evaluation throughout the game",
    subtitle = "White's advantage — positive means white is better",
    x      = NULL,
    y      = "White's advantage",
    color  = "To move"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

### Features

```{r}
featsL <- sch |>
  select(feature, matches("^f[0-9]+$")) |>
  pivot_longer(-feature, names_to = "t", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(move = as.integer(sub("^f", "", t)),
         color = ifelse(move %% 2 == 0, "white", "black"))

ggplot(featsL, aes(move, value, color = color)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = .4) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, alpha = .6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#4A2C17", "#E8D5B7")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 7)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  facet_wrap(~feature, ncol = 1) +
  faceted_quarto +
  labs(title = "Feature values by move")
```

### Weights

```{r}
wtsL <- sch %>%
    select(feature, starts_with("w")) %>%
    pivot_longer(-feature,
                 names_to="t",
                 values_to="value") %>%
    mutate(move=rep(0:7, 3))

ggplot(wtsL, aes(move, value, color=feature)) +
    geom_point(size = 1, alpha=.5) +
    geom_line(linewidth=1, alpha=.8) +
    scale_color_viridis_d() +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:7) +
    facet_wrap(~feature, ncol=1, scales="free_y") +
    faceted_quarto +
    labs(title="Weights by move")
```

## Interactive walkthrough

Step through the game with the buttons or slider. Each position shows the board alongside the feature values, weights, and contributions for that ply.

```{r ply-viewer, include=TRUE}
# Replay the game to build a board for each ply
sans <- c("e4", "e5", "Bc4", "Nc6", "Qh5", "Nf6", "Qxf7#")
ply_labels <- as.character(traj$label)

game_board <- chess_m$Board()
ply_boards <- vector("list", length(sans) + 1)
ply_boards[[1]] <- game_board$copy()
for (i in seq_along(sans)) {
  game_board$push_san(sans[[i]])
  ply_boards[[i + 1]] <- game_board$copy()
}

ply_panels <- lapply(seq_along(ply_boards) - 1, function(k) {
  htmltools::div(
    class = "ply-panel",
    style = if (k == 0) "display:block;" else "display:none;",
    render_ply(ply_boards[[k + 1]], paste0("f", k), paste0("w", k),
               feats_df = sch, wts_df = sch)
  )
})

label_js <- paste0("[", paste0('"', ply_labels, '"', collapse = ","), "]")

htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::div(
    style = "display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:center; margin:12px 0;",
    htmltools::tags$button(id = "ply-prev", type = "button", "Previous"),
    htmltools::tags$button(id = "ply-next", type = "button", "Next"),
    htmltools::tags$input(id = "ply-slider", type = "range", min = 0,
                          max = length(ply_labels) - 1, step = 1, value = 0,
                          style = "flex:1;"),
    htmltools::tags$span(id = "ply-label", ply_labels[1])
  ),
  ply_panels,
  htmltools::tags$script(htmltools::HTML(paste0(
    "(function() {",
    "  var panels = document.querySelectorAll('.ply-panel');",
    "  var slider = document.getElementById('ply-slider');",
    "  var label = document.getElementById('ply-label');",
    "  var labels = ", label_js, ";",
    "  function show(i) {",
    "    i = Math.max(0, Math.min(panels.length - 1, i));",
    "    panels.forEach(function(p, j) { p.style.display = (j === i) ? 'block' : 'none'; });",
    "    slider.value = i;",
    "    label.textContent = labels[i];",
    "  }",
    "  document.getElementById('ply-prev').addEventListener('click', function() { show(parseInt(slider.value) - 1); });",
    "  document.getElementById('ply-next').addEventListener('click', function() { show(parseInt(slider.value) + 1); });",
    "  slider.addEventListener('input', function() { show(parseInt(slider.value)); });",
    "})();"
  )))
)
```
